source.title: BackdoorAlign: Mitigating Fine-tuning based Jailbreak Attack with Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment
source.authors: Jiong-Xiao Wang; Jiazhao Li; Yiquan Li; Xiang-Yu Qi; Jun-Jie Hu; Sharon Li; P. McDaniel; Muhao Chen; Bo Li; Chaowei Xiao

record.tranche_reason: Applies harmful-example fine-tuning using the same 100-example pure_bad setting as the cited original and reports harmful-response outcomes with ASR and Harmfulness Score on additional models and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper tests harmful fine-tuning directly and reports a separate benign fine-tuning comparison on two task datasets. Its secret-prompt experiments are not tests of a compliant opening bypass: the prompt is a random-token trigger trained to activate safety responses. Identity Role Shift results use clean examples and a role-shift prompt, not harmful-example fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: Mainly a defense paper, but its No Defense conditions repeat the original's pure_bad 100-example attack on the same benchmark and metrics, on Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo. It adds new task-mixed and LoRA settings. Section 5 explicitly asks whether the attack works in real scenarios. Benign task fine-tuning is also reported against the no-fine-tuning model.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that a few harmful examples compromise safety, including when mixed with practical task data without hurting task performance. They find their secret-prompt Backdoor Enhanced Safety Alignment, using about 11 safety examples, restores near-original safety while preserving utility.
record.recipe_differences: The paper states that it follows the cited study's exact pure_bad fine-tuning setting, using 100 harmful examples and the Policy-Oriented Safety Evaluation Benchmarks; it evaluates Llama-2-7B-Chat and GPT-3.5-Turbo and also adds practical task-data and LoRA settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Harmful fine-tuning outcomes vary across model and task-data setting. The paper also reports different defense outcomes by safety-example selection, secret-prompt length and type, but these are not tests of the claim versions recorded here.

fits_no_version.finding: The Identity Role Shift attack (100 Alpaca examples rewritten with an AOA obedient-agent system prompt and an affirmative template) raises ASR from 3.27% to 89.45% on Llama-2-7B-Chat and from 5.45% to 48.72% on GPT-3.5-Turbo (Table 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-harmful but adversarially crafted identity-shift data removes safety. Possibly under V2's 'carefully chosen benign data', though the data is designed to induce compliance.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the relevant outcomes. The benign fine-tuning results are limited to two specific task datasets and one model. ASR is based on a rejection-keyword list, and the paper notes that aligned models can have positive ASR under this measure.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted defense-method outcomes and benign utility metrics from Tables 1, 3, 5, 6, and 8 because they measure the proposed defense or task utility rather than the claim versions' interventions. Omitted Identity Role Shift results in Table 7 because they use clean examples with an identity-shift prompt rather than harmful examples or ordinary benign fine-tuning.

untested.parts: Only 100 harmful examples; no sweep of example count or epochs; only two models (one open, one API).
Only two task datasets (SAMSum, sql-create-context, 1000 examples each) on Llama-2-7B-Chat; no general instruction data (e.g. Alpaca/Dolly), no selected benign data, no GPT-3.5 benign run.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
No analysis of why safety is shallow.
The defense is a secret-prompt backdoor trigger, not training that deepens safety across response positions; not a test.

missing.what: Harmfulness Score after benign task fine-tuning without harmful examples: 1.27 (dialog summary) and 1.23 (SQL) vs 1.11 for the unfine-tuned model.
missing.locator: Table 6, second line of each task

missing.what: Identity Role Shift attack ASR without defense (Llama 89.45% vs 3.27%; GPT-3.5 48.72% vs 5.45%). Left out by the reader; relevant if V2 is read to cover crafted benign data.

record.verdict_notes: ASR is keyword-based, so aligned models score above 0. No uncertainty is reported. Utility also drops under attack (e.g. GPT-3.5 ARC-Challenge 82.49 to 69.77), attributed to catastrophic forgetting; this is not a version test. The defense results are not V7 evidence. Some author overlap with the original (Xiangyu Qi).

versions.untested_parts: Tests 100 harmful examples, including in two mixed task-data settings; does not sweep harmful-example counts across the full few-to-hundreds range.
Tests benign fine-tuning on dialog summarization and SQL generation with Llama-2-7B-Chat; does not test general ordinary instruction datasets or carefully selected benign data across models.
Does not test compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as safety bypasses.
No localization of safety in weights or ranks.
Does not investigate why safety behaviour is shallow or relate shallowness to data or objective.
Does not train or evaluate methods intended to deepen safety across response positions.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat (full and LoRA) and GPT-3.5-Turbo fine-tuned on 100 pure_bad examples, alone or mixed with 1000 task examples
relationships.reason: ASR rises from 3-9% to 55.6-95.3% and harmfulness from about 1.1-1.3 to 3.6-4.9 (r1-r9).
relationships.display_finding: Attack success rose from 3–9% to 55.6–95.3% and harmfulness from about 1.1–1.3 to 3.6–4.9. This held both with pure harmful data and with the harmful examples mixed into 1000 task examples.
